ei.title: Building the Earth One Atom at a Time
ei.subject: 9월_2023 고1 모의고사
ei.lesson: Building the Earth One Atom at a Time

fullPassage: Maybe you've heard this joke: "How do you eat an elephant?" The answer is "one bite at a time." So, how do you "build" the Earth? That's simple, too: one atom at a time. Atoms are the basic building blocks of crystals, and since all rocks are made up of crystals, the more you know about atoms, the better. Crystals come in a variety of shapes that scientists call habits. Common crystal habits include squares, triangles, and six-sided hexagons. Usually crystals form when liquids cool, such as when you create ice cubes. Many times, crystals form in ways that do not allow for perfect shapes. If conditions are too cold, too hot, or there isn't enough source material, they can form strange, twisted shapes. But when conditions are right, we see beautiful displays. Usually, this involves a slow, steady environment where the individual atoms have plenty of time to join and fit perfectly into what's known as the crystal lattice. This is the basic structure of atoms that is seen time after time.

questions.passage: Atoms are the basic building blocks of crystals, and since all rocks ①<u>are</u> made up of crystals, the more you know about atoms, the better. Crystals ②<u>come</u> in a variety of shapes that scientists call habits. Many times, crystals form in ways that do not ③<u>allow</u> for perfect shapes. But when conditions are right, we see beautiful displays that ④<u>is produced</u> in a slow, steady environment.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.analysis:
① are: 'all rocks are made up of ~'로 복수 주어(rocks)에 맞는 동사예요 — 적절.
② come: 'Crystals come in ~'로 복수 주어(Crystals)에 맞는 동사예요 — 적절.
③ allow: 'do not allow'로 do 뒤 동사원형이라 적절해요.
④ is produced → are produced: 선행사가 beautiful displays(복수)이므로 관계절의 동사도 복수 are produced가 맞아요. is produced는 단수라 틀려요 ←정답
det.tip: 관계절 동사는 선행사(displays, 복수)에 일치 → are produced

questions.passage: Maybe you've heard this joke: "How do you eat an elephant?" The answer is "one bite at a time." So, how do you "build" the Earth? That's simple, too: one atom at a time. Atoms are the basic building blocks of crystals, and since all rocks are made up of crystals, the more you know about atoms, the better. Crystals come in a variety of shapes that scientists call habits. Common crystal habits include squares, triangles, and six-sided hexagons. Usually crystals form when liquids cool, such as when you create ice cubes. Many times, crystals form in ways that do not allow for perfect shapes. If conditions are too cold, too hot, or there isn't enough source material, they can form strange, twisted shapes. But when conditions are right, we see beautiful displays. Usually, this involves a slow, steady environment where the individual atoms have plenty of time to join and fit perfectly into what's known as the crystal lattice. This is the basic structure of atoms that is seen time after time.

questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
